candidates.title: Canonical hashes depend on the riscv64 binutils/base image used to build the uarch; nothing pins them or checks the pristine hash against an expected value
candidates.component: uarch program build (uarch/Makefile, Dockerfile toolchain stage, generated uarch/uarch-pristine-ram.c and uarch-pristine-hash.c)
candidates.role: Honest operator (uarch program and its pristine state are part of the transition function, R13); on-chain pristine-hash constant is generated from it (referee verifier constant)
candidates.location: Dockerfile lines 1-15 (BUILD_BASE=debian:trixie-20250811 by tag only; only gcc-riscv64-unknown-elf=14.2.0+19 and g++-14-riscv64-linux-gnu=14.2.0-19cross1 pinned; binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, which assembles and links uarch-ram.bin, floats with the archive); uarch/Makefile (uarch-pristine-ram.c and uarch-pristine-hash.c regenerated by xxd/compute-uarch-pristine-hash from whatever toolchain is on PATH; top-level 'make uarch' uses the host riscv64 toolchain); uarch/.gitignore (both generated files untracked); no committed expected UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH anywhere in src/, uarch/ or tests (grep finds only the harness and the runtime constant).
candidates.description: The uarch RAM image is in the hashed state (every root hash covers it, and every uarch reset restores it), so its bytes are part of every canonical hash. Those bytes are compiler/assembler/linker output. The build pins gcc but not binutils (the harness rebuild reports binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf 2.44-3+7+b1 'NOT pinned') and the base image is pinned by mutable tag, not digest. A non-Docker 'make uarch' uses any local riscv64 toolchain. The build never compares the resulting pristine hash against an audited constant, so a toolchain drift silently yields an emulator with a different UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH and different canonical hashes for every state, and a regenerated machine-solidity-step with a different constant. The emulator's version check (marchid/mimpid) cannot detect it because the machine-identification registers do not change.
candidates.trigger: No adversary: whoever builds the emulator (operator or release engineer) after a Debian archive update of binutils-riscv64-unknown-elf, or with a non-Docker toolchain.
candidates.reachability: Not a guest-state issue; reachable on the honest operator's path 'the emulator binary and its build' whenever the build environment drifts. Today the harness rebuild reproduces 0x89ae34ba...43d7, so the drift is latent.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The trust boundary says 'the emulator binary and its build' is trusted, which could exclude a mis-built node; but R13 requires 'The uarch program, its pristine hash, and the verifier code that a deployment fixes on-chain must be reproducibly buildable from audited source', so the build recipe itself is in scope.
2 Role: uarch program / pristine state = honest operator per AUDIT.md table ('uarch program'); its hash becomes the referee verifier constant (EmulatorConstants.sol UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH).

3 High/Medium cases: section 8 High lists 'A uarch program or verifier code fixed on-chain that cannot be reproducibly rebuilt, while what is deployed matches its audited source.' It matches only once the floating binutils (or base image) changes the output; today the rebuild matches, so the case is conditional.

4 Critical: R1 'must not depend on ... Compiler or optimization level' is the angle, but R13 explicitly makes the uarch program and its pristine state part of the protocol, so the dependency is governed by R13's reproducibility clause rather than R1; no reachable-state violation today.
5 Low otherwise: a real defect in build reproducibility (unpinned toolchain component, no expected-hash check).
candidates.claimed_severity: Low today; High (section 8, non-reproducible uarch program) as soon as an unpinned toolchain component changes the uarch-ram.bin bytes
candidates.threat_to_goal: If two honest builds of the same audited tag disagree on uarch-ram.bin, at most one matches the deployment's on-chain pristine hash; the other computes wrong canonical hashes for every claim (completeness failure for that operator) and nothing in the emulator flags it except a player that compares with the chain (crisium.lua does; production nodes may not).
candidates.evidence: Read Dockerfile and uarch/Makefile; grep shows no tracked expected pristine hash; bugs/harness/work/uarch-rebuild/report.txt records binutils 2.44-3+7+b1 as unpinned and all hashes currently agreeing.
candidates.test_idea: A test that builds the uarch in the pinned toolchain image and asserts (a) every package that produces uarch-ram.bin bytes (binutils included) is version-pinned and the base image is digest-pinned, and (b) the build fails unless the computed pristine hash equals a committed constant; it fails today on (a)/(b) because neither exists.

candidates.title: Whether a configuration with a read-only flash drive is accepted depends on the host page size
candidates.component: os::mapped_memory (os-mapped-memory.cpp) used by memory_address_range for flash drives / NVRAM; machine creation from a configuration
candidates.role: Honest operator (creating the valid template from a configuration; storing/loading are not affected)
candidates.location: src/os-mapped-memory.cpp, mapped_memory constructor: partial_page_size = backing_file_length % page_size (host mmap page size); 'if (flags.read_only) throw possible non zero partial page'; src/memory-address-range.cpp check_mmap_flags: read_only = host_read_only && !newly_created(), backing_gap = !shared
candidates.description: When a flash drive is read-only and its image file is shorter than the drive (allowed for unshared drives: the gap is anonymous zero memory), creation throws if the file length is not a multiple of the HOST page size. On a 4 KiB-page host an 8192-byte image in a 1 MiB read-only drive is accepted; on a 16 KiB (macOS/Asahi arm64) or 64 KiB-page host the same configuration is refused. The resulting machine, when created, has the same contents everywhere (zero gap), so no hash differs; only acceptance depends on the host OS/CPU page size.
candidates.trigger: Operator or template author using a read-only flash drive whose image is smaller than the drive length and a multiple of 4 KiB but not of the host page size.
candidates.reachability: Requires a template configuration with such a drive and a non-4 KiB-page host; stored machines are unaffected (stored data files have the full length).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No exclusion matches; not a snapshot, not an API misuse.
2 Role: machine creation = honest operator path ('Obtaining its valid template').

3 High/Medium: no wrong hash or proof; it 'fails loudly'. Section 8 Medium lists 'A persistence operation that fails loudly ... in an uncommon host setup that the manual documents' (only if the manual documents such hosts; creation is not strictly persistence).

4 Critical: R1 'must not depend on ... Host OS, CPU' is about the canonical hash, which does not differ; R4 'A configuration that would not [hold the rule] is rejected when the machine is created' is respected (it is rejected at creation).
5 Low: 'a portability gap on an unsupported host'.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (Medium if 16 KiB/64 KiB-page hosts are documented as supported)
candidates.threat_to_goal: Does not threaten the goal: an operator on such a host cannot create the template but gets an error, never a different hash.
candidates.evidence: Ran exp_ro.lua (scratch R1 dir) on this 4 KiB host: 1000-byte image -> 'possible non zero partial page' error; 8192-byte image in a 1 MiB read-only drive -> created (root 0xf85e1499...). By code, 8192 % 16384 != 0 makes the same config throw on a 16 KiB-page host.
candidates.test_idea: Unit test of mapped_memory with a mocked page size (or run on a 16 KiB-page host) asserting that a read-only mapping whose file length is a multiple of 4096 is accepted (the gap zero-filled without writing, e.g. by mapping the tail page anonymously).

candidates.title: Unreproducible mode is read from the configuration copy, not the hashed iunrep, and write_reg can change the hashed iunrep after creation
candidates.role: Honest operator API (write_reg); plausibly not called by a production node with iunrep
candidates.location: src/machine.hpp is_unreproducible(): 'return m_c.processor.registers.iunrep != 0'; src/machine.cpp write_reg case reg::iunrep: 'm_s->shadow.registers.iunrep = value' (no read-only check, unlike marchid/mimpid/mvendorid); consistency is checked only at construction (validate_processor_shadow).
candidates.description: R2 asks that 'Every register and every configuration value that affects a transition has one source of truth in the hashed state, and every path reads it from there' and R14 that 'The unreproducible mode is fixed at creation and recorded in the hashed state'. The native paths (poll_external_interrupts, collectors, log producers, store) decide reproducibility from the configuration copy m_c, while the hashed state holds shadow iunrep. write_reg(iunrep, x) changes the hashed register without changing behavior, so the state commits to a mode the emulator does not run; storing then writes config iunrep=0 next to shadow iunrep!=0, which no longer loads ('iunrep mismatch').
candidates.trigger: A trusted machine-API caller writing iunrep after creation.
candidates.reachability: Only through the machine API; the guest cannot reach iunrep (R8).
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope: section 8 excludes 'The effect of a deliberate state change made through the machine API, when the API performs it as documented'. The manual calls iunrep 'a creation-time mode', so a write that the API accepts arguably is not 'as documented'; still a trusted-caller action.
2 Role: machine API (honest operator only where a node plausibly calls it; it would not write iunrep).

3 Medium? 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves ... the cached state of the machine or a stored directory inconsistent with the machine's contents (R9)' fits loosely (stored directory becomes unloadable).
5 Low: 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'.
candidates.threat_to_goal: None for a correct operator; it violates the single-source-of-truth wording of R2/R14.
candidates.test_idea: write_reg('iunrep', 1) on a reproducible machine must be refused (or is_unreproducible must read the shadow register); the test asserts write_reg raises.

not_covered: Exhaustive UB audit of soft-float.hpp (only clz/shift/normalize paths reviewed; no UBSan run over FP test vectors, riscv-tests FP binaries are not built in the harness)
Native vs uarch differential runs (R2) on edge cases; I relied on reading the interrupt/stop-resume invariants instead of fuzzing
